answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and registers one kernel, a program seeded by its key. Each epoch it runs the kernel on the seed and files the pearl, graded on a pearl-grade table; only outputs reaching the zenith band count. An auditor recomputes the run from the seed and key, so a copied pearl hashes differently and burns the bond. First run 38 credits; the kth costs 38+7(k-1), since runs are keyed separately, unbatchable; the 1000th costs 7031, so 1000 fakes cost 3,534,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-kernel ring fails: the seed follows the renter's key. An honest agent pays 38 once.
